items.text: sendAddGuestsEmails can leak hidden notes to attendees by not respecting hideCalendarNotes setting
The server never checks that guest emails within one request are unique. A direct tRPC call with duplicate addresses creates duplicate attendee rows and sends duplicate emails.
Spread `props` before the fixed template props, otherwise callers can override this email's subject, title, and header.
New guests are saved with name '' and inherit the organizer's timeZone/locale, so emails and calendar entries show blank names
Duplicate guest emails are not removed from the input list

Line 168 passes the original unfiltered guests array to sendAddGuestsEmails instead of uniqueGuests, causing existing attendees to receive wrong email template (AttendeeScheduledEmail instead of AttendeeAddGuestsEmail)
Guest list has no server-side size cap and no server-side uniqueness check; a direct tRPC call can create duplicate attendee rows and send unbounded mail in the organizer's name

The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.

The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.

Dialog state bugs: isInvalidEmail never reset on success or on overlay/Esc close; closing via onOpenChange keeps old emails; removing all fields makes Add a silent no-op; client uniqueness check is case-sensitive
Permission check isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...) collapses to owner-only; team ADMINs who are not organizer/attendee get FORBIDDEN despite the variable name isTeamAdminOrOwner

The blacklist comparison lowercases the blacklisted emails but not the incoming `guest` email. A user can bypass the blacklist by submitting an email with different casing (e.g., `Blocked@example.com`).
Empty fragment <></> in MultiEmail can be simplified by restructuring the conditional
No tests are included for the new handler or UI components
sendAddGuestsEmails ignores the event type's disable-host/attendee-email settings; handler does not pass booking.eventType?.metadata
BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS filter is bypassable by case change or +alias; existing-attendee de-dup is also case-sensitive, so A@x.com is added beside a@x.com
Server never checks booking status or time: guests can be added to CANCELLED, REJECTED or past bookings, sending REQUEST/CONFIRMED ICS invites that revive dead meetings
MultiEmail is a near-verbatim copy of the multiemail factory in packages/features/form-builder/Components.tsx, creating code duplication that will drift

The isTeamAdminOrOwner check uses `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)` which reduces to owner-only, so team ADMINs who are not the organizer or an attendee get FORBIDDEN. The variable name is also misleading.
No server-side deduplication of guest emails, allowing duplicate attendee rows to be created for the same booking since there's no unique constraint on (bookingId, email)
sendAddGuestsEmails ignores disableStandardEmails flags and forwards calendarEvent unchanged, which can send emails when they're disabled

`uniqueGuests` only filters against existing booking attendees and the blacklist, but does not deduplicate the input `guests` array itself. Submitting the same email twice in the request will create duplicate attendee records.
uniqueGuests doesn't actually de-duplicate the guests input and compares emails case-sensitively, allowing duplicates or case-variant blacklist bypasses to be inserted/sent downstream
The server never checks booking status or time. Guests can be added to CANCELLED, REJECTED or past bookings, which writes attendee rows and sends REQUEST/CONFIRMED ICS invites for a dead meeting.
In onError, message is always a non-empty string (often starting with undefined:), so the unable_to_add_guests fallback will never be used and the toast can be confusing
Invalid email banner remains visible even after user edits the email input to valid values - banner only clears when clicking Cancel or attempting to add again
Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.
evt is built without team, so the team-member branch in sendAddGuestsEmails never runs and team hosts are never notified

The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.
Handler passes raw guests instead of uniqueGuests to sendAddGuestsEmails, so a re-submitted existing attendee gets a fresh 'scheduled' email instead of the 'guests added' notice
showAttendees is never passed to AttendeeScheduledEmail, so seated events with seatsShowAttendees=true hide the attendee list in these emails

There is no seated-event handling. Attendee rows are created without BookingSeat rows, which bypasses seatsPerTimeSlot. The full attendee list is then pushed to the organizer's calendar event, which can expose seat-holders to each other when seatsShowAttendees is false.
Notifications use the unfiltered guests input instead of the filtered uniqueGuests list
findFirst include pulls user.credentials (full credential keys) that are never read, and trips @calcom/eslint/no-prisma-include-true
onSuccess resets multiEmailValue but not isInvalidEmail, so reopening the dialog after a previous validation failure can immediately show the error state again

The permission check uses `&&` (AND) instead of `||` (OR). This requires the user to be both a team admin and a team owner simultaneously, which is almost never true. A team admin or team owner should each independently have permission to add guests.
addGuests uses plain authedProcedure with a custom check instead of bookingsProcedure: any logged-in attendee may add guests, while COLLECTIVE co-hosts are refused

Seated events (seatsPerTimeSlot): attendees are created without BookingSeat rows, bypassing the seat limit, and any single seat-holder can add guests exposing seat-holders to each other even with seatsShowAttendees=false

Authorization logic bug in addGuests.handler.ts:47 - isTeamAdminOrOwner uses && instead of ||, so only team owners pass the check while team admins are incorrectly denied access despite isTeamAdmin already covering both ADMIN and OWNER roles
isTeamAdminOrOwner uses && between isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner, which requires user to be OWNER and blocks ADMIN users from adding guests

sendAddGuestsEmails function does not check eventTypeMetadata.disableStandardEmails, which is inconsistent with other email-sending functions and could result in unwanted emails for event types that have explicitly disabled standard emails
~40 lines of CalendarEvent building duplicated from editLocation.handler.ts
New authenticated mutation that writes to the DB, calls external calendars and sends email ships with zero tests
Second prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow refetches the organizer already loaded via booking.user
Email uniqueness check in ZAddGuestsInputSchema is case-sensitive, so User@x.com and user@x.com pass as unique
Authorization check uses && requiring both admin AND owner roles, which blocks legitimate admins or owners who only have one role - should use || instead
Seat bookings need seat-level scoping, but this new action updates by `bookingId` only. On seats events it can add guests to the shared booking instead of the current seat.

sendAddGuestsEmails receives the raw guests input instead of the filtered uniqueGuests, so an existing attendee re-submitted alongside a real new guest gets a fresh 'scheduled' email instead of the 'guests added' update.

`sendAddGuestsEmails` is called with the raw `guests` input instead of `uniqueGuests`. This means notification emails may be sent for guests who were already attendees or were filtered out by the blacklist.
Guest emails are not normalized (case/base-email) before blacklist comparison, allowing bypass of BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS with different casing or plus-addressing
Handler throws FORBIDDEN with message key you_do_not_have_permission, which is not defined in en/common.json; users see the raw key
The error-toast fallback can never trigger because the template string `${code}: ${t(msg)}` is never falsy, so unable_to_add_guests is dead code and users see raw error codes.

No transaction/compensation: attendees are written before updateCalendarAttendees, which is not wrapped; if it throws, DB has the guests, no emails go out, and retry fails with emails_must_be_unique_valid
addGuestsHandler requires user to be BOTH team admin AND team owner (using && instead of ||), blocking team admins who are not owners from adding guests to team bookings
onError message is a template string that is never falsy, so the unable_to_add_guests fallback never shows and users see raw 'CODE: key' strings
Using array index as key in MultiEmail can cause issues when items are removed from the middle of the list
sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests) uses the raw input rather than the filtered list that was actually added, which can misclassify new vs existing attendees and send the wrong email type
MultiEmail.tsx imports primitives from @calcom/ui while living inside packages/ui, which risks circular imports now that @calcom/ui also exports MultiEmail
De-duplication against existing attendees is case-sensitive, so `A@x.com` can be added next to an existing `a@x.com`.

The BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS filter can be bypassed by changing the case of an email or adding a plus-alias, because the raw guest is checked without applying extractBaseEmail or toLowerCase normalization.
Reassigning function parameter 'value' in MultiEmail component is a code smell

The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.
MultiEmail component uses useLocale() hook but is missing the 'use client' directive, which can break Next.js App Router usage when rendered from a Server Component
EventManager is built from ctx.user's credentials, not the organizer's; references without credentialId are matched against the caller's calendars when an attendee or owner adds guests
Guest email comparisons are case-sensitive, allowing blacklisted/existing guests to slip through with different casing

uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.

issues.claim: In addGuests.handler.ts, the team permission check uses `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)` where `||` is intended. This reduces it to an owner-only check, so team ADMINs who are not the organizer or an attendee get FORBIDDEN even though the variable is named isTeamAdminOrOwner.

The BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS check lowercases the blacklist but compares it against the raw guest email, with no toLowerCase or extractBaseEmail normalization. Blacklisted addresses therefore pass when submitted with different casing or a plus-alias.
De-duplication against existing booking attendees is case-sensitive, so `A@x.com` can be added next to an existing `a@x.com`.

The server does not de-duplicate the input guests array (uniqueGuests only filters existing attendees and the blacklist). A direct tRPC call with repeated emails creates duplicate attendee rows and sends duplicate emails, and there is no unique constraint on (bookingId, email) and no server-side cap on list size.

The handler passes the raw `guests` input to sendAddGuestsEmails instead of `uniqueGuests`. As a result, existing or filtered attendees are classified as new and receive the wrong email (AttendeeScheduledEmail instead of AttendeeAddGuestsEmail), and notifications go to guests who were not actually added.

sendAddGuestsEmails does not check the event type's disableStandardEmails settings, and the handler does not pass booking.eventType?.metadata. Emails are therefore sent even when standard host/attendee emails are disabled.
sendAddGuestsEmails does not respect the hideCalendarNotes setting, so hidden notes can be sent to attendees.
`props` is spread after the fixed template props, so callers can override the email's subject, title and header.
New guests are saved with an empty name and inherit the organizer's timeZone/locale, so emails and calendar entries show blank names.

In the add-guests dialog, isInvalidEmail is not reset on success or on overlay/Esc close, so the error state can reappear when the dialog is reopened. Closing via onOpenChange also keeps the old emails, removing all fields makes Add a silent no-op, and the client uniqueness check is case-sensitive.
The invalid-email banner stays visible after the user edits the input to valid values. It clears only on Cancel or on another add attempt.
MultiEmail contains an empty fragment `<></>` in a conditional.
No tests are included for the new addGuests handler/mutation or the new UI components.
The server does not check booking status or time. Guests can be added to CANCELLED, REJECTED or past bookings, which writes attendee rows and sends REQUEST/CONFIRMED ICS invites.
MultiEmail is a near-verbatim copy of the multiemail factory in packages/features/form-builder/Components.tsx.
In onError, the toast message is the template string `${code}: ${t(msg)}`, which is never falsy. The unable_to_add_guests fallback is therefore never used, and users see raw 'CODE: key' strings.
The email list state starts as an array containing an empty string rather than an empty array.
evt is built without `team`, so the team-member branch in sendAddGuestsEmails never runs and team hosts are not notified.
showAttendees is not passed to AttendeeScheduledEmail, so seated events with seatsShowAttendees=true hide the attendee list in these emails.

There is no seated-event handling: attendee rows are created without BookingSeat rows, which bypasses seatsPerTimeSlot. The full attendee list is pushed to the calendar event, and any seat-holder can add guests, exposing seat-holders to each other even when seatsShowAttendees is false.
The new action updates by bookingId only, without seat-level scoping, so on seats events guests are added to the shared booking instead of the current seat.
The booking findFirst include pulls user.credentials (full credential keys), which are never read, and trips @calcom/eslint/no-prisma-include-true.
addGuests uses plain authedProcedure with a custom check instead of bookingsProcedure. Any logged-in attendee can add guests, while COLLECTIVE co-hosts are refused.
About 40 lines of CalendarEvent construction are duplicated from editLocation.handler.ts.
A second prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow refetches the organizer that is already loaded via booking.user.
The email uniqueness check in ZAddGuestsInputSchema is case-sensitive, so User@x.com and user@x.com pass as unique.
The handler throws FORBIDDEN with message key you_do_not_have_permission, which is not defined in en/common.json, so users see the raw key.

There is no transaction or compensation: attendees are written before updateCalendarAttendees, which is not wrapped. If it throws, the DB keeps the guests, no emails are sent, and a retry fails with emails_must_be_unique_valid.
MultiEmail uses the array index as the React key, which misbehaves when items are removed from the middle of the list.
MultiEmail.tsx lives inside packages/ui but imports primitives from @calcom/ui, which also exports MultiEmail, creating a circular import risk.
The MultiEmail component reassigns its function parameter `value`.
The MultiEmail component uses the useLocale() hook but lacks the 'use client' directive.
EventManager is built from ctx.user's credentials rather than the organizer's. References without a credentialId are matched against the caller's calendars when an attendee or owner adds guests.
